_comment: What demo imagery this theme needs, and the prompt for each piece.
250 elements do not need 250 photographs. They need a small pool that the
demo content reuses, which is also how a real site works: one photo library,
many pages. Each entry is generated once into Resources/Public/Images/<pool>/
and referenced from library.json / fixture.json as an EXT: path.
Two providers, chosen per pool rather than globally. Anything with lettering
in it goes to Gemini's image model, which renders text far more reliably;
everything else goes to GPT Image 2, which is cheaper per picture. See
The businesses named here are the inventions the demo copy already uses.
None is real, and no prompt asks for a real company, product or person.

style.shared: Editorial photography for a business website. Natural light, muted colours, shallow depth of field, no text or logos anywhere in the frame, no watermarks. Documentary rather than staged stock: real work in progress, imperfect surfaces, unposed. 16:9 unless stated.
style.portrait: Head-and-shoulders portrait of a fictional person, natural window light, plain uncluttered background, neutral friendly expression, looking at the camera. Not a glamour shot; the register of a company's own staff page. Square crop.
style.logo: A flat vector wordmark on a plain white background. One or two colours, no gradients, no photographic elements, generous margins. It must read as a small business's real mark, not as clip art.

scene.purpose: The general-purpose photo pool behind the 65 elements with a single image field.

images.prompt: A tidy workshop bench in a small metalworking shop, hand tools laid out, afternoon light from a high window.
A service technician in workwear checking a rugged tablet beside an industrial boiler in a plant room.
A narrow warehouse aisle of shelved parts boxes, a picking trolley mid-aisle, cool overhead light.
Four colleagues standing around a monitor in a small open-plan office, mid-discussion, papers on the desk.
A trade counter in a wholesaler, an order form and a card reader on the worktop, shelves behind.
A plain white delivery van with its rear doors open on a quiet industrial street at dawn, crates inside.
Two surveyors with a tripod-mounted instrument on the edge of a construction site, overcast sky.
Hands spreading a large technical drawing across a table, a scale rule and a pencil resting on it.
A single half-populated server rack in a small utility room, cables neatly combed, door ajar.
A modest training room with a semicircle of chairs and a flipchart, empty before a session.
An early-morning bakery counter, trays being loaded, a till at the end of the run.
A small cafe interior just after opening, chairs down, one member of staff at the espresso machine.
A calm physiotherapy practice reception, appointment screen off to one side, plants and light wood.
An empty physiotherapy treatment room, plinth made up, exercise bands hung on the wall.
A utility control desk with several monitors showing generic line diagrams, one operator seated, back to camera.
A small electricity substation behind a mesh fence in open countryside, late afternoon.
Freshly installed copper pipework and valves against a plant-room wall, insulation part-fitted.
A river monitoring station on a shallow gravel-bed stream, a measuring post in the water, trees behind.
A researcher in waders taking a water sample into a bottle at a riverbank, notebook on the bank.
A modest water-testing laboratory bench, sample bottles in a rack, a pipette in use.
Two people at the corner of a meeting table with a laptop between them, mid-conversation, glass partition behind.
A set of keys and a signed job sheet being handed across a doorway threshold on a residential landing.
Rooftop ventilation plant against a grey sky, access walkway in the foreground.
A lit workshop window seen from outside at dusk, someone working inside, rest of the street dark.

logo.purpose: Wordmarks for the invented companies the demo copy names. Generated with the same model as the photography: Gemini renders lettering more reliably, but a second provider is a second key, a second bill and a second failure mode for twelve pictures. Check the spelling on every one — see the note in the README.
